In 2021 @thechrisdo took my speaking fee from $1,000  to a $5,000 minimum. It wasn’t just a tactical adjustment. It was an identity shift 🤯

And I realized that is what I was missing all along. Did the strategies and tactics help me streamline my business? Absolutely. But I was missing an IDENTITY piece. I was missing the “I am worthy” piece of the puzzle 😭

Once I had that, I was actually able to implement more of the strategies Chris had given me content, branding, and lead generation over the years.

And that’s the thing I’ve learned most about, not only from the retreats and masterminds …

Most businesses don’t have a marketing problem. They have a positioning problem.

If you’re trying to sell to everyone, you’re probably selling to no one.

Personal Branding & Business Coach Chris Do breaks down why getting more specific is the fastest way to get more customers.

Watch the full conversation on BigDeal.

When I tell people I’m building the most trusted brand in the world for design agency owners, they almost always say the same thing:

“Oh, you’d be great at that. You’re the second person I always think of for that stuff.”

I ask them who the first is.

“@thechrisdo,” they answer.

I told Chris I was coming for him, and he said, “Bring it.”

Then I asked him if he would help me, and he said, “Absolutely.”

Three months ago, I sat with Chris for two days and he shared everything he could with me in the time we had together. He gave generously and didn’t hold back. That’s the kind of person he i…

Look closely at this photo. Notice what I'm doing???
It LOOKS like diligence... but it's actually AVOIDANCE.

I'm the one on the right, head down on my laptop at Chris Do's freaking Casa Dojo! It was the BEST SEAT I've ever had with him: extra time to talk and a REAL CHANCE at one-on-one coaching in person.

I've followed Chris for almost a decade and hosted him TWICE in Vancouver... Yet I STILL felt like I had to be on my best behavior around him.

So I retreated into the work. I polished a document. I cleaned up my prototypes. I packaged my business ideas.

It LOOKED like prudence.
It LOOKED…

Purgatory for Asian Kids 😂

🎙️: ⁨Chris Do

Drop a comment and I’ll DM you this whole episode!!!

Brands die in the middle.

Most people think good branding means appealing to more people.

So they soften the edges.
They try to be premium and affordable.
Bold and safe.
Exclusive and accessible.

The problem?

When you stand for everything, you stand for nothing.

Strong brands make decisions.

They choose where they sit on the spectrum—and they’re willing to go all the way to a 1 or a 10.

Where is your brand still playing it safe in the middle?

Since we opened our doors, we’ve watched you move slowly through the living galleries, pause in The Sanctuary, and wear a scent that existed nowhere in the world until your own emotions made it. DATALAND was built on a simple, stubborn dream: that art could be not only shown to you, but grown — from the living world, and from you. It rests on the Large Nature Model, an AI we…

This acquisition marks a grand milestone in our studio’s journey and also for digital art. It inscribes a historic chapter as MoMA welcomes the first Generative AI and tokenized artwork into its esteemed permanent collection.

profile.name: Aaron James Draplin
profile.headline: Late Shift Foreman, Draplin Design Co.
profile.summary: Aaron is a veteran graphic designer and the founder of Draplin Design Co., known for his deep appreciation of Americana, classic typography, and handmade craftsmanship. He has spent over three decades in the industry, working with major brands like Nike and Field Notes while maintaining a prolific personal output of logos, fonts, and workshops. His public persona is that of a warm, humorous, and dedicated mentor who finds joy in the 'making' process and the history behind everyday objects.
profile.career: Founder of Draplin Design Co. and a long-time partner in the Field Notes brand, where he has served in a quality control and creative capacity for over 20 years. He also runs a successful business selling over 400 merch items and offers design workshops and Skillshare classes.
profile.lifestyle: Aaron spends his time in Portland, Oregon, balancing high-volume production of design goods with teaching and speaking engagements. He is actively involved in the local design community, participating in events like Portland Design Month and AIGA Portland, and frequently shares his creative process and studio life with his large social media following.
needs: A partner who appreciates the creative process and the value of 'making' things by hand.
Someone who is supportive of his demanding schedule, which includes late-night work ('Late Shift Foreman') and frequent travel for workshops.
A person who shares his love for history, Americana, and the stories behind objects.
A partner who is comfortable with his public-facing role and large social media presence.
dealbreakers: Disrespect for craftsmanship or the value of handmade goods.
Lack of humor or inability to appreciate his self-deprecating wit.
Indifference to the creative community or the importance of mentorship.
High-maintenance expectations regarding his time, given his 30+ year career of high-volume production.

latestPosts.caption: GREEN THEORY I’ve always considered the view beyond the windows part of the interior composition. Here, the garden sets the chromatic tone within. A mélange of olive, moss, and sage creates a richly layered setting for sculptural forms, rare vintage discoveries, and works by emerging designers... 1990s aluminum armchairs by Mats Theselius, a contemporary side table by Michael Anastassiades, and an Art Deco cabinet by Rudolf Lorenz. An unexpected dialogue between eras, materials, and perspectives, where contrast brings the composition to life. XK
LAST COUPLE WEEKS XK

ALTITUDE ADJUSTMENT Alpine season is almost here! Beefbar in Courchevel is such a special project with my studio. A contemporary interpretation of alpine vernacular with a nod to the sculptural spirit and understated glamour of the 1970s. Cypress timber, patinated copper and bronze bring warmth, texture and an unexpected edge to high-altitude design. Can’t wait for the season to begin! XK

FALLING FOR IT ALL Vintage obsessions, emerging designers, established fashion houses, and a few things I absolutely do not need but cannot resist. I love the tension between old and new, the unexpected pairings, and pieces with a little attitude. What I’m loving this fall, what’s on my list, and what’s already found its way into my closet.
Full story now live on WEARSTLERWORLD. XK

PETITS TRÉSORS When in Paris, I always love to stop by Galerie Édouard de La Marque on Rue de Lille on the Left Bank. It makes me so happy. Warm, distinctly Parisian and full of charm, with one person’s eye running through it all. From Roger Capron’s tiled tables to Mithé Espelt’s glazed mirrors and jewel boxes, the ceramics are a study in scale, surface and color. I came home with a beautifully glazed square dish and have my eye on a gold mirror for the Malibu house. XK

BIRDS OF A FEATHER The invitation arrived as a bird necklace... and then the birds appeared overhead at the Grand Palais. Loved the poetry of that. @Matthieu_Blazy’s Chanel collection had so much to take in. The flowing dresses, the shoes, the bags, the unexpected color combinations, the proportions, and all those tiny, thoughtful details you only really understand when you see them move. It felt light, playful, and incredibly considered. Such a beautiful night. Thank you @ChanelOfficial for including me. XK

#ChanelSpringSummer #CHANELShow

ACQUISITION INSTINCT In Paris for a show and some work, with a little room for curation in between. A stop at @jacqueslacoste turned up a few pieces I fell hard for. Already imagining where they might land. XK

Photography: @eseniyaa
Wearing: @chanelofficial shoes and bag, @knwlslondon skirt, @celine blazer, Enrose blouse

POWER OF MULTIPLES Spent some time with @aurelienserre at Marché Serpette in Paris. I love how each dealer has their own point of view, their own collector’s eye. What drew me in at Aurélien’s was his taste for rare pieces and, of course, repetition. One of my obsessions. The way objects are grouped, repeated, placed in conversation. You see each piece differently when you see it in multiples. XK

publications.description: This cookbook is an inside glimpse into how one of the world’s top chefs cooks in his home kitchen for those nearest and dearest to him. publications.title: Yes, Chef: A Memoir
publications.description: It begins with a simple ritual: Every Saturday afternoon, a boy who loves to cook walks to his grandmother’s house and helps her prepare a roast chicken for dinner. The grandmother is Swedish, a retired domestic. The boy is Ethiopian and adopted, and he will grow up to become the world-renowned chef Marcus Samuelsson. This book is his love letter to food and family in all its manifestations.

I travel a lot and these are the 10 THINGS I DO ON EVERY FLIGHT: 

1. Hydrate before I get to the airport.
I start early so I’m not playing catch-up once I’m in the air.

2. Add electrolytes to my water.
Especially on longer flights. It helps me arrive feeling less depleted.

3. Walk the terminal instead of sitting at the gate.
I’m about to sit for hours, so I use that time to get some movement in.

4. Put an AirTag in my checked luggage.
I like knowing where my suitcase is before the airline does.

latestPosts.caption:
Today is World Mental Health Day. And we’ve made great progress in recent years raising awareness and opening up the conversation about mental health.

This year, I hope we take it one step further: mental health is brain health. A growing body of research shows how our brain health connects to everything from daily brain fog and anxiety to long-term cognitive decline.

So here’s a Microstep to try today: take a moment to check-in with your own mental health by naming the feeling you’re having right now in one word. Simply putting a feeling into words can help calm the brain’s stress response.…

AI keeps pulling off things that used to be impossible. In my latest On My Mind newsletter, I write why we shouldn’t lose sight of the eight “wonders of life,” as coined by @UCBerkeleyOfficial professor Dacher Keltner, that create everyday moments of awe: moral beauty, movement, nature, music, visual design, spirituality and religion, big ideas, and life and death.

Plus, dispatches from @Dreamforce, the @LucasMuseum, and my own home, where I recently hosted an event that captured the possibility of this moment when it comes to brain health.

You can read my newsletter at the link in bio.

Wise words, whether we’re elite athletes competing at the highest levels or building healthy habits in our daily lives. Congrats to @CaitlinClark22 — @WNBA Comeback Player of the Year! — on a great season, and thank you for your deep commitment to helping people live healthier lives by putting a spotlight on healthy behaviors, including the role of exercise as one of the most powerful preventative medicines, and reminding us all to start how we can.

As @ariannahuff pointed out, our generation rarely talked about menopause when we were younger. But we’re shouting it from the rooftops now, because women deserve better—not only from the health care system, but from their workplaces too. #menopauseawarenessmonth 

Read more about the @gallup x @pivotaldotcom survey on women’s health at the link in my bio.

“The more we share…the more we can accelerate the shift in the culture.” Couldn’t agree more, @ariannahuff.

Thanks for a great conversation on the need to make women’s health more visible.

Arianna Huffington (@ariannahuff) has a message for the people in Silicon Valley who think they are building God.

Watch or listen on Futurology. Link in bio.

What a beautiful story of hope in The @Guardian. Twenty-one years ago, a field in Norfolk was home to a single crop. Today, it is a wildflower meadow with more than 150 plant species. Since 2011, the only maintenance has been one hay cut each summer. The cut keeps the field from becoming woodland and gives more delicate wildflowers room to grow.

As @UCL Professor Carl Sayer put it: “Sometimes we’re not patient enough.” And after watching the meadow become more biodiverse each year, he says, “It’s hope — we can recover things. We just need to do less in the recovery process.”

Life is a dance …

latestPosts.caption:
Rewinding to my conversation with Simon Sinek. ✨

What if giving up was actually the thing that helped you find your way forward?

In my conversation with Simon Sinek, he shared a powerful story about the moment he stopped fighting so hard for a particular outcome—and what happened when he finally surrendered.

Sometimes, letting go doesn’t mean you’re giving up on your life or your dreams.

Sometimes, it means making space for what comes next. ✨

Want to hear Simon’s full story? Comment SURRENDER and I’ll send you the episode. 👇

Some words stick with you.

Over the years, I’ve collected a few quotes that genuinely changed the way I think, work, and move through life. 💭

These are a few I still come back to, because sometimes the right words at the right time can change everything.

Swipe through, and tell me: which one do you need to hear right now? 👇

Sometimes the voice telling you to quit is wisdom. Sometimes it’s fear, doubt, exhaustion, or the discomfort of doing something that actually matters. 💭

The trick is learning to tell the difference.

Before you give up, pause. Get curious. Ask yourself what’s really going on—and what you actually want.

What's something you quit that turned out to be a blessing? Tell me in the comments. 👇

Throwing it back to my conversation with Lewis Howes. 

There’s a big difference between easy money and making money easy. 💰

In my conversation with Lewis Howes, we talked about the temptation to chase the shortcut—the next big opportunity, the get-rich-quick promise, the thing that looks like easy money.

But “easy money” can come with a very expensive lesson.

Making money easy is different. It’s about building the skills, experience, and systems that make creating wealth more sustainable over time.

Want to hear the full conversation with Lewis? Comment MONEY and I’ll send you the episode…

Quick question: How many sales might you have lost when the right person landed on your website, opened your email, or saw your post…
…but your words didn’t click? 😬

Great copy isn’t about sounding clever, polished, or “professional.”
It’s about knowing how to write words that connect, persuade, and sound unmistakably like YOU.

Because in a noisy world,  writing that connects is a SUPER POWER.
And the good news? It’s a skill you can learn. 🙌

I created a FREE 7-Day Writing Class to help you do exactly that.
Comment WRITE and I’ll send it your way. 💌

And P.S. — if you’re ready to go much …

Rewind to one of my favorite conversations. 💭

What if the thing you’ve been taught to see as a weakness is actually pointing you toward your greatest strength? 

In my conversation with Bryce Dallas Howard, we talked about how her learning disability shaped the way she sees herself, her strengths, and the way she works.

Sometimes the thing that makes you feel different can become the very thing that helps you find your path. ✨

Want to hear the full conversation with Bryce? Comment GIFT and I’ll send you the episode. 👇

Some weeks are full of wins.
Others are just about making it to the other side.

Whatever this week held for you, you made it through. And that counts. 🤍

Take a breath. Give yourself some credit. Now enjoy your weekend.

Happy October! 🍂🎃
There’s something about this time of year I just love. The summer travels wind down, the pace gets a little slower, and sweater weather gives me an excuse to cozy up and actually sit still for a minute. 😂

So I made myself an October bingo card with a few of my favorite fall things! 🎃👻🍁

latestPosts.caption:
✨🦄 NEW PR AT THE BOSTON MARATHON!!! 🦄✨

3:27:37
7:55/mile pace
Four minute PR from my best previous time at Berlin 2024

Honestly, still speechless over this. I cannot believe that at age 44, one week after a 100k race, five months post-injury…that this happened. An entire marathon at a mile pace that starts with a 7! A Boston Qualifying time AT BOSTON! And to do this with my son here with me! OMFG!!! 

Have been working so so hard, and it doesn’t always come together on race day. But when it does…there’s no feeling quite like it. 

Time to go eat all the food and cry so many happy tears.

Fastest Known Time on the Baja Sur 135km Trail! 

On March 6, I attempted the Fastest Known Time (FKT) for Mexico’s 135km Baja Sur Trail across the entire Baja Sur Peninsula. 

82 miles from the Pacific Ocean → Sea of Cortez.
13,000 feet of elevation.
One absolutely savage mountain section from miles 17–34 that climbed 6,000 feet in just 6 miles — including three straight miles at 30% grade in peak heat.
40 miles through night under the moon and stars.
One 5-minute dirt nap after mile 60.
And a sunrise at mile 70 that made the entire effort feel almost spiritual.

My first “comeback” ultra dis…

Officially a @cocodona250 finisher.
Still processing the experience and will have a more in depth post soon, but for now: 

257 miles across Arizona
36,000+ feet of elevation
6 total hours of sleep across 5 days
Torrential rain, insane heat, snow, lightning & hail
Insane amounts of Coca Cola & cookies consumed
65 miles done on a busted shin/ankle
Hysterical laugher and full body crying 
Met my own soul (several times)
Literally the greatest friends on the planet

latestPosts.caption:
Congrats to @adamgrant on the publication of VIBE! There’s nothing better than a book that walks through your brain and rearranges the furniture!

I love that we now have names for different kinds of friendships and a deeper understanding of how we need all of these: associates, allies, pals, and companions. And, as one of my awesome UT grad students pointed out, I appreciate that this taxonomy is not about progression - they’re all important to us for different reasons.

Congrats again @adamgrant - Vibe is a total vibe!

@aclfestival is here and I get to talk to one of my favorite artists @lolayounggg. Join us on the Bonus Tracks stage tomorrow for a conversation about vulnerability, creativity, and the power of messy.

Deeply grateful to @adamgrant, our podcast team, @voxmedia, and all of you who watched and/or listened! I learned way more than I offered and for that I’m very thankful! And, last - Adam and I will be together in Dallas for the Vibe book launch later this month and taking on a fun topic in January on his pod! CAN NOT WAIT!

Thanks again, everyone!
BB❤️

When we see people attack empathy or say things like, “The fundamental weakness of Western civilization is empathy” (Elon Musk, 2025), we should ask ourselves, “What harm, pain, or hurt do they not want us to see or feel? Who do they want to hurt, humiliate, or dehumanize without accountability?”

Based on our research over the past 25 years, creating meaningful connections and human-centered systems requires a combination of compassion and cognitive empathy. I think of compassion as the daily practice and cognitive empathy as one its most powerful tools.

We define compassion as the daily pra…

This is one of my favorite @thecuriosityshop episodes. In a world where everyone and everything is fighting for our attention, our rage, and our money, we exam what makes us vulnerable to persuasion and how we can develop stronger influence literacy skills. 

It’s the best kind of collision between Adam’s, “think like a scientist” research and my work on shame and vulnerability. 

Biggest finding: 
Shame around being persuadable makes us more vulnerable to influence. Acknowledging that we are vulnerable to those reels and TikTok’s and snake oil pitches makes us more resistant! 

If you want to…

@adamgrant and I loved talking with @angelalduckworth about her new book, “Situated.”

Big takeaway:

“To stay motivated through the countless hours of practice that separate amateurs from experts, grit is necessary but not sufficient. The situation also matters—and to an astonishing degree:

Culture matters.
Mentors matter.
Teammates matter.
Even the objects in your personal space matter.

How you think about your goals and what you’re willing to do to achieve them depends on both you and your situation.”

I also loved our conversation about billboards - those signs we post around our spaces …

To my Longhorn family: Try not to step in the bullshit left behind by small-minded people.
Stay strong. Like UT vs OSU strong. 🧡🤘🏻🤍

Priya Parker, one of my favorite thinkers and writers, is joining @thecuriosityshop this week and we’re talking about fighting! Not “dukes up” fighting but how real heat and conflict can build connection if we’re willing to learn how to do it well.

What I love about this conversation and Priya’s new book - “The Art of Fighting” - is being called to imagine a world where we unlearn and relearn what it means to gather and to disagree. And, she’s just so honest and fun!

To watch or listen to the full episode, head to YouTube or wherever you listen to podcasts.

profile.summary: Brené Brown is a distinguished research professor and author, known for her work on vulnerability, courage, and leadership. Her warm, empathetic tone invites listeners and readers to explore deeper human connections.
